ONE POT MATAR PANEER!!! 

Probably, my favorite Indian meal has got to be garam matar paneer with phulka and this recipe makes the absolutely best healthy indulgence anyone could want! 

Recipe mentioned below! 

To make the Masala paste, you need to blend together
15 cashews
6 black peppercorns
3 cloves
2 green cardamom
Pinch of cinnamon powder
4 sprigs of coriander leaves
2 medium tomatoes
1 onion
2 green chillies
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste

In a pressure cooker, heat 1 tbsp ghee (use oil to make this vegan), Add 1 tsp cumin and saute till it becomes aromatic. 
Then add in your Masala Paste and cook for 10 – 15 minutes (the more you cook this paste, the flavours will develop more. Once the paste has thickened and become a deeper colour, add in ¼ tsp haldi + 1 tsp red chilli powder + ½ tsp garam masala powder and combine. 
Follow that up by adding 150 grams of green peas (I use Safal frozen) + 1 cup water, use more if you like a thinner gravy and pressure cook the mix for 10 minutes. Let the cooker release on its own and stir the gravy. Add in a Pinch of Salt  and 200 grams Paneer - I've used @idfreshfood ( use Tofu to make this Vegan) + 1 tsp crushed kasturi methi. Serve with a sprinkle of coriander leaves!

This homemade spicy salsa can be made using a food processor and ready to serve in 5 minutes. 
This is perfect for light snacking with nacho chips and as an accompaniment in an indulgent mexican dish. 

This recipe is VEGAN!

Ingredients: 
2 medium tomatos
1 onion
2 green chillies
a few sprigs of coriander leaves
the juice of one lemon
1 tsp cumin powder
1 tsp grounud black pepper
1/2 tsp red chilli powder

Add all your ingredients to a food processer and combine. 
You can drain out any excess liquid ( this way you dont need to deseed your tomatos and use everything up)

I use the @amazondotin food processor and it's so sturdy even when i overfill it sometimes 😅

Mexican Week continues with this amazing Mexican Rice also known as Arroz Rojo.
Recipe mentioned below ⬇️

This recipe is perfectly vegan and is a tangy dish consisting of long grained basmati rice, cooked in tomatoes along with simple onion, capsicum and spices. 
You can all any vegetables you want to the rice to increase the nutritional value. 

Recipe: 
- 1 tbsp oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 8 cloves of garlic, chopped
- 200 grams basmati rice
- 1 bell pepper, chopped into cubes
- 2 green chillies, finely chopped
-1  tsp cumin powder
- 1 tsp red chilli powder or paprica powder
- 180 grams tomatoes, blended
- pinch of salt
- 550 ml, warm water or vegetable stock

Optional vegetables: 2 vegetables maximum else reduce quantities of each

- 1/2 cup carrot, cubed
- 1/2 cup green peas
- 1/2 cup cauliflower
- 1/2 cup sweet corn
- 1/2 cup french beans

Method: 
-start by rinsing and then soaking your rice for 30 minutes
-heat oil in the pan and add in the onion and garlic to saute
-add in your rinsed rice and saute for a few minutes on a low heat
-add in your vegetables, green chill, chilli powder, cumin powder and salt
-stir the mix for 3-5 minutes and proceed to add in your blended tomato puree after that
-add in your warm water, cover the mix and allow it to cook for 20 minutes until all the liquid has been absorbed and you have a fluffy mix.

First step to the perfect tres leches starts with a simple sponge cake.

i completely get if someone doesnt or cannot eat eggs, but baking with eggs is always better and this sponge cake is the answer to that debate always!!

Part two drops tomorrow!!

Ingredients: 
- 75 grams AP Flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- pinch of salt
- 3 eggs
- 120 grams caster sugar ( 90 grams for yolk and 30 grams for egg whites) 
- 50 ml milk
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

Method: 
- seperate your eggs.
- whip your egg whites with sugar till stiff peaks for, and set aside. 
- using the same beater, in another bowl, add in your egg yolks, sugar, vanilla and beat untill light and airy. the mix will change colour
- add in your flour, baking powder and salt and fold through followed by your milk to form the mixture. 
- slowly, in parts, as shown in the video, fold your egg whites into the mix till they are incorporated only. DO NOT OVERMIX OR DEFLATE THE MIX. 
- add the mixture into a 8 inch cake ring or 8 inch square baking dish that has been greased and lined with parchment paper. 
- bake at 180 degrees for 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted inside comes out clean.

Pastel de Tres Leches

a super light cake soaked in three types of milk. 
traditionally this cake has condensed milk, evaporated milk and heavy cream however i have used standard milk instead of cream to keep the mix slightly lighter. 

Ingredients: 

- sponge cake - 1 portion (recipe in the previous reel)
- evaporated milk - 177 ml ( boil 350 ml of milk for 20 minutes till it reduced to half and strain) 
- condensed milk - 200 ml
- milk - 60 ml
- heavy whipping cream - 60 - 80 ml ( DO NOT USE AMUL CREAM)
- pinch of cinnamon

Method:

- mix all three milks together. 
-poke holes in the sponge cake and add all three milks.
- allow the cake to soak for a minimum of 4 hours to overnight
- whip your cream till medium peaks and top your cake with it. 
- sprinkle with a pinch of cinnamon and enjoy :)

ONE POT PALAK PANEER

Ingredients:
Spinach Mix:
- 250 grams spinach, stems removed, blanced for 1 minute
- 2 green chillies
- a small piece of ginger
- 10 garlic cloves

For the Palak Paneer:
-1 tbsp oil
- 1 bayleaf
- 1 tsp cumin seeds
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
- pinch of hing
- salt to taste
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- 1/2 tsp garam masala powder
- 1 tsp fresh cream
- 200 grams paneer OR Tofu
- 1 tsp kasturi methi, crushed

Recipe: 
- add your blanched spinach, green chillies, ginger and garlic to a mixer and blend together till smooth
- in a saucepan, add in your oil and heat, followed by the cumin and bayleaf.
- add in the onion and saute till translucent, then add in your tomato, red chilli powder, hing, turmeric powder and garam masala
- add in your spinach paste followed by a 1/4th cup of water and cook for a few minutes
- add in your fresh cream and mix again
- add in your paneer and coat with the spinach mix, cook for another few minutes
- add in garam masala and saute for a minute followed by your crushed kasturi methi

Punjabi Kadhi is always a good idea! 
a flavourful tangy yogurt based curry that comes together in under 20 minutes. 
It has minimum prep work and only requires some onions to be cut up to prepare :) 

Recipe mentioned below! 

Kadhi Mix: 
- 400 grams of dahi ( sour dahi works best for this recipe)
- 1 tsp red chilli powder
- 1 tsp turmeeric poweder
- 1 tsp garam masala powder
- pinch of hing
- 1.5 tsp salt
- 40 grams besan (gram flour) 
- 3 cups of water

FOR KADHI: 
- 1 tbsp mustard oil
- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds
- 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera)
- 1 tsp methi seeds (fenugreek) 
- pinch hing
- 1 tbsp ginger + 1 2 cloves of garlic
- 1 onion, sliced
- 2 green chillies, slit

Method: 

- Add all your Kadhi Mix in the blender and blend till smooth ( do not over mix here as the curd can curdle while cooking or break up during blending, you need a smooth texture), set aside
- in a pan, heat your oil and add in your mustard seeds, cumin seeds & saute
- add in hing and methi seeds next and allow it to saute till flavourful
- add in your onions and mix till translucent 
- follow that up with your slit green chillies and saute for a few minutes
- add in your Kadhi blended mix and mix together. allow your mix to cook for 10 - 15 minutes till it thickens and the colour deepens. 
- take off the heat and top with chopped corinader leaves

MY POTATO ROAST RECIPE
(URLAI ROAST) (VEGAN)

Ingredients
- 5 Potatoes, boiled, peeled and chopped
- 2 tsp oil
- 1.5 tsp mustard seeds (rai)
- 1 tsp turmetic powder
- 1 tsp red chilli powder
- 2 tsp sambar powder (heaping tsps)
-  pinch of salt
- 10 curry leaves
- 2 tbsp water 
- coriander leaves to garnish

Method: 

- Start by boiling, peeling and then chopping your potatoes into your favorite size pieces
- in a pan, add in your oil followed by mustard seeds and let them pop. 
- add in your potatoes and coat them lightly follow that up with haldi, red chilli powder, sambar powder and salt. 
- toss this together on medium high heat. PRO TIP: you can add in little water here to mix the masalas better and gives you a crispier crust on the potatoes as it fries. 
- add in curry leaves and serve it fresh :)

VEGAN MASALA PAV is always a good idea! especially when you have leftover pav at home. 

Ingredients:
Chilli Paste: 
6 cloves of garlic+2 slivers of ginger+2 green chillies crushed together

For the Masala, 
- 1 tsp oil 
- 1 tsp cumin seeds
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 tomatoes, finely chopped
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- 1/2 tsp red chilli powder ( mild not kashmiri)
- 2 - 3 tsp pav bhaji masala powder ( easily available in supermarkets or online) 
- 1/2 cup warm water
- pinch of salt

For the Pavs:
- 1 tsp oil for sauteeing the pav OR 1 tbsp butter
- 3 OR 4 pavs, sliced in halves ( you can take off the slight coning on the top half of the pav for a flat piece)

To Garnish: 
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- coriander leaves, chopped
- 1 lemon, to finish

Optional: 1 - 2 tbsp of hung curd whipped to cut the spice and masalas :) 

Method: 

- Start by making your chilli paste.
- In a pan, add in your oil and cumin seeds allow them to splutter
- follow that up with your chilli paste and cook till the raw smell is gone
- add in your onions and saute 
- once your onions turn translucent, add in your tomatoes and cook for a few minutes
- add in all your powders at this stage - turmeric, red chilli and pav bhaji masala along with your salt. 
- add in your capsicum after that and saute for 2-3 minutes
- add in your water and cook for 5-6 minutes allowing the mix to thicken up and reduce. 
YOU DO NOT WANT THE MIX TO BE WATERY AS THIS WILL IMPACT YOUR FINAL DISH
- remove your masalas from the pan and add 1 tsp of oil. 
- to the oil, add your pavs and roast them till they are crisp and soft. 
- take them off the pan and top with masala, chopped onions, coriander and a squeeze of lemon :)

CHOCOLATE CHIP BANANA BREAD 
READY IN 30 MINUTES!! 

All you need is 2 bowls, a whisk and a spatula to make yourself an amazing Banana bread. 

Recipe below ⬇️

Ingredients: 
Dry
- 120 grams Ap flour
- 75 grams caster sugar
- 20 grams brown sugar 
( If replacing both sugars, you can use 90 grams of jaggery powder) 
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- pinch of salt
- 1/2 tsp cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp nutmeg

Wet:
- 2 ripe bananas, mashed (feel free to use a third banana if you have it) 
- 1 egg, beated
- 57 grams oil ( vegetable or ghee or melted butter), room tempreture
- 1 tbsp vanilla essence
- 100 grams chocolate chips ( i use @callebautindia OR you can use 50 grams nuts +  60 grams of chocolate chips

Method: 
- combine your dry ingredients in a bowl and whisk together
- in a new bowl, add in all your wet ingredients and mix well together
- add your wet ingredients to the dry and fold together slowly ( never over mix your batter when there is maida involved as overmixing will result in a dense cake)
- add in your chocolate chips and do a few more gentle folds
- 
Baking : 
Tempreture : 170 degres for 20 - 25 minutes
remember to keep checking post the 20 minute mark

Vessel: 
I have used 2 5-inch cake tins.
This recipe can be made in 4 mini tins or double the recipe for a 9 * 5 tin to make a loaf

THE BEST COOKIE DOUGH #1 - 
SMORES COOKIES

Easy, Instant and no prep work required. this cookie dough comes together in minutes and can be baked instantly after its ready. 

Disclaimer: Since its summer in India, tempretures are high all around. i do recommend refridgerating this dough for 20 minutes before stuffing and 40 minutes after you stuff them 🥰

Ingredients: 
for the base:
- 57 grams butter, softened 
- 80 grams brown sugar
- 25 grams caster sugar
- 1 egg, straight from the fridge is fine :) 
- 1 tsp vanilla essense

Dry: 
- 150 grams AP flour, sifted is ALWAYS better
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp salt

Mix ins: 
100 grams of chocolate
1 medium mashmallow per cookie
25 grams crushed biscuits 
i used 75 grams of hersheys creamy milk chocolate and 25 grams of @callebautindia chips because dark chocolate is BETTER always
for the biscuits, i used a simple digestive

Method: 
- add all your dry ingredients together, seive them and set aside
- cream your butter slightly with a spatula and then add in your sugars and bring together
follow that up with your cold egg and 1 tsp. this mix needs to be whipped with a whisk for 1 - 2 minutes
- gently fold in your dry mix and when your dry mix is almost fully incorporated, add in your chocolate along with your crushed biscuits and bring the dough together. 
- scoop out one ice cream scoop size of dough, stuff the dough with 1 or 2 mashmallows depending on their size and seal the dough
- refridgetate your dough balls for around 40 minutes till slightly firm. 
- preheat your oven at 170 degrees C
- bake in the oven for 10 - 14 minutes. keep checking your cookies after the 8 minute mask and when the sides seem to be firming up and the centre is still soft, they are ready
- put the oven on broiler and put the cookies back in for a minute, watch them so the mashmallows get a slight colour and take them out
- THE HARDEST PART: leave them to cool for 15 minutes on the sheet and dig in ;)

My signature Ella's Tips are mentioned on the blog :) 

Ingredients: 
- 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

- 6 small tomatoes OR 4 medium tomatoes, deseeded and cut into cubes
- 1 tsp salt
- 10 basil leaves, sliced thin
- 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar ( i like 3 tbsp because BALSAMIC IS THE BEST)

Method:

- while the mix is chilling, toast your bread in the oven at 180 degrees c until it gets crispy
- top with your tomato mix and serve it fresh.

FLOURLESS CHOCOLATE CAKE

this gluten free dessert is the perfect centre piece of 2 OR 4 not so greedy guests

Ingredients:
- 60 grams butter, i use @amul_india
- 85 grams dark chocolate, 55% or more, i used @allthingschocolates
- 70 grams caster sugar
- 1 tsp coffee powder, i use @brucoffeein
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 2 eggs
- 13 grams cocoa powder, i use @vanhoutenprofessional
- 1/2 tsp salt

Ganache topping: 
- 100 grams chocolate, your choice milk or dark, again using @allthingschocolates
- 80 grams heavy cream, using @amul_india

Method: 

-Melt your chocolate and butter together, this can be done on a double boiler or in the microwave. allow it to cool while you weight out your remaining ingredients

- add your sugar + coffee + vanilla into the cooled chocolate mix and whisk it together ( you will see small specks of sugar which hasnt dissolved, that is okay)

- crack your eggs into the batter one by one till both the eggs are incorporated. do not worry if your batter seems a little curdled, once the 2nd egg is in, the batter will have a shiny look

- finally, fold in your cocoa + baking powder + salt gently till well combined

- pour your batter into your mould. we have used a 5 inch tin here. if using double this recipe, you will need a 6 or 7 inch tin for a thicker cake

- place the cake tin into a preheated oven. 
IMPORTANT: next to your cake tin, add in another tin with boiling water to create steam in the oven. this will result in the best texture for this cake 

- bake the cake for around 20 minutes till the cake is properly cooked but please ensure that you do not over bake this. at the 15 minute mark, make sure you check the cake with a thin knife. a few crumbs or little batter is okay. 

- cool in the fridge for 1 hour and its ready to eat.

This Makhni Gravy will blow your mind!!!! 
its healthy, super easy to make vegan ( just dont add butter) and is ready in under an hour. 

I found the biggest advantage is that you can cool the gravy down, box it and freeze till you need it on a rainy day :) 

Ingredients: 
Spices: 
8 garlic cloves
3 cardamom pods, green
3 cloves
6 kashmiri red chilli, dried
1/2 tsp cinnamon powder

Gravy: 
2 tbsp oil or 1 tbsp oil + 2 tbsp butter
1 onion, chopped
1/2 kg tomatoes, around 9 medium sized , chopped
a handful of cashew nuts 
1 tsp red chilli powder
1 tbsp of ketchup
1 heaping tbsp on kasturi methi
salt, to taste as per your preferece

Method:
- In a large pan, add in your oil or butter and allow it to heat slightly
- add in your spices as mentioned above and saute them till they start turning colour. if using butter, the butter will start to turn to a dark brown do not worry as this is due to it having a lower smoke point than oil, also, it adds flavour
- add in your onion then and saute till translucent. 
- follow that up with your tomatoes + cashew and allow the mix to cook covered for 10 - 15 minutes till your tomatoes are super soft and cooked through
- let this mix cool down slightly and blitze till smooth. you can add a few tbsp of water at this point.
- add your blended mix back on the stove and heat it. add in your red chilli powder + tomato puree paste + salt +1/4 cup warm water and mix . Let this cook for another 10 - 15 minutes ( you will see the gravy getting a slightly darker colour)
- at this stage, you can add in your cooked tandoori chicken or tandoori paneer to make a butter chicken / butter paneer. 
- top with kasturi methi, stir it in and switch off the gas

Storage: this gravy freezes well on its own without any chicken or paneer for upto 2 months.

7 ingredients, under 30 minutes :) 

Ingredients: 
Dry
- 140 grams AP Flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- pinch, salt

Rest of the Ingredients:
- 120 ml milk + 1 tsp vinegar
- 60 grams of softened butter
- 100 grams of caster sugar
- 1 tsp vanilla essence

Method: 
- preheat your oven to 170 degrees C

- sift the dry ingredients together
- in a seperate bowl, cream the butter and sugar till it gets white in colour then add vanilla

Flour - Buttermilk - Flour - Buttermilk - Flour
- DO NOT OVERMIX
- Divide the batter into a cupcake pan lined with cupcake liners. you should get 8 cupcakes. fill a little more then half way full
- Bake for 15 minutes else till a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. 
- take out of the pan, cook on a rack and front when ready :)

LAVASH RECIPE 

Get ready to impress yourself and your guests with this simple wholewheat lavash recipe :) 

Ingredients
- 2 cups whole wheat flour
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup of warm water
- 1 tsp salt
- 1.5 tsp red chilly powder

For topping
- 1 - 2 tsp white sesame seeds
- 1 - 2tsp nigella seeds

Method: 
- preheat the oven to 190 degrees celsius
-  in a bowl, combine Flour + Salt + Red chilli powder
- add in the oil and mix gently followed by the water and kneed the dough together
- divide the dough into 4 equal parts and cover with a towel on the counter and allow to rest
- in the meantime, lightly flour your counter. take one ball of dough and use a belan to roll it into the desired shape
- transfer your dough to the sheet tray
- using a pizza cutter, cut the  dough into the desired shape, brush some olive oil on top and sprinkle both the seeds. 
- pat the seeds into the dough so they dont fall off post baking :) 

Storage: 
In an airtight container for 2-3 weeks

Jay Fai, Bangkok

Jay Fai is a Bangkok street food institution that should be a must visit during your trip to Thailand.
In 2018, she got her first Michelin star and has maintained it till date while being ranked in the 100 best restaurants in the world!!! 

A few key points to note 
- you will be waiting a minimum of 1-2 hours for your table, so put your name on the list outside and note the number you have on the list 
- You can walk around the area while you wait for your number but don’t go too far though, as you might miss your turn and will need to go back to the bottom of the list
- Order everything you want all at once

What we ate 
- Crab Omelette - priced at 1200 Baht, it is an expensive option but something everyone recommends and I totally get why
- Drunken Noodles - priced at 600 Baht, these are a must have in my books. The noodles she uses are insane and the sauce compliments the perfectly cooked vegetables and jumbo prawns
- Orange Juice - priced at 70 baht per glass. I had 3 so enough said ;) 

Pro tip: while you're waiting for your table to be seated, go across to Thipsamai right next to Jay Fai for their orange juice. While they make the most legendary Pad Thai in the city, the orange juice was a perfect combination of pulp and juice, priced at 160 baht per big bottle 

Overall 
We waited in line for around an hour and everyone seems to tell me that’s quite a minimum for this restaurant, so we might have gotten lucky.
The food is not cheap by any means but if you have ever eaten at one of the best rated restaurants in the world (Jay fai is currently rated 85th in the whole entire universe right now) with a Michelin star (I haven’t), I would say it’s a pretty steal deal!!!

This Kada Prasad recipe is one for the ages. 
I asked an aunty of mine to share the recipe they use at home to make it as authentic as possible. 

This is at the most basic level a whole wheat halwa that will blow you away and is ready in under 20 minutes!!!

Ingredients: 
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 100 grams, sugar ( caster or regular sugar works) 
- 60 grams whole wheat flour (1/4 cup)
- 1/2 cup ghee (works out to around 75 grams)
- 2 - 3 cardamom cloves

Method: 
- start by making your sugar syrup by combining the water + sugar + crushed cardamom over medium heat and allow it to boil
- in a heavy bottom sauce pan, add in the ghee and allow it to melt over low heat 
- add in the whole wheat flour and mix it together with the ghee. stir over medium heat for a few minutes till the mix gets a deeper colour
- add in your sugar syrup in two parts straining out the cardamom pods
- mix it over gentle heat for a few minutes , top it with cashews or almonds and serve :)

Ingredients

Mushroom Ragù Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil / butter 
- 3 tbsp garlic, finely chopped
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 tbsp celery stem, finely chopped ( coriander is an alternative here but it doesn’t lend the same aromatic depth as celery)
- 1 red carrot, finely diced
- 200 grams button mushrooms, finely chopped ( i use my pigeon chopped- 5-6 pulls works well) 
- 2 tomatoes, pureed OR 2 tbsp tomato paste
-salt+pepper+oregano+chili flakes
- 1 cheese slice ( you can use grated cheese as well) Cheese is always subjective in a recipe, add as little or as much as you want
- 1-2 tbsp cream, you can add a 1 tbsp more if needed for a creamier finish
- 120 grams pasta, any type of pasta works well with this recipe :) 

Optional:
Increase protein in the meal by adding -cooked chicken, paneer, tofu. 

Method: 
- add oil to a pan and add in your onion, garlic, celery and saute for a few minutes
- add in your carrot and stir, add in your mushroom
- while the water is releasing add in your salt, pepper, oregano & chilli flakes and cook till the filling dries out
- add in your tomato puree / paste and cook for 15-20 minutes for puree and 10 minutes if using paste
- while the sauce is cooking, boil your pasta, i use whole wheat which takes around 15-18 minutes to cook properly
-add cheese and cream to the sauce and stir to combine.

Chocolate Soufflé Recipe 
Makes 4 

Ingredients: 
-57 ml milk
-30 grams sugar, divided equally ( half for custard mix + half to whip egg whites)
-pinch of salt
-1 tbsp maida
-15 grams butter, cubed, if using salted butter, omit salt from the recipe
-80 grams chocolate, 70% and up works best
-2 eggs, seperated
-1/2 tsp vanilla essense
-pinch of cream of tartare, skip if you do not have
-butter + caster sugar for buttering and dusting the ramekin

Method:
-using a pastry brush, brush the ramekins with butter and add the sugar moving it around till the bottom and sides are evenly coated
-add flour + sugar + salt to a saucepan, add in milk and stir together till combined, then add in the butter and stir on a low flame till everything is disolved and slightly thickened. 
-add in your chopped chocolate and stir till melted and combined, allow to cool slightly before adding in your egg yolks. once combined, leave to cool
-in another bowl, add your egg whites + cream of tartare. whip your egg whites while gradually adding in the 15 grams of sugar till you achieve stiff peaks
-fold the egg whites into the chocolate custard in 2 parts folding the mixture gently so you dont reflate it too much
-add your mix to the ramekins and bake in a preheated oven (190°C) for 10-12 minutes or until your souffle has risen well and is not jiggly
-remove from the oven and serve immediately

Coffee Hazelnut Biscotti Recipe 🌰☕️🍫
Desserts from A-Z, the goal : to try to make desserts i have never made before. the key word here is try and we are on B for Biscotti. 
why do most of the biscotti recipes have almonds, they are probably my least favorite nut out there. this biscotti recipe is full of my favorite flavours coffee, chocolate, hazelnuts and spices !the best part you dont need any fancy equipment to make these and they have a great shelf life! 

Ingredients 
-1 tbsp coffee powder + 28 ml hot water - allow to cool
-2 tsp milk
-1 small egg, room temp ( you can attempt to replace the egg by using 35-40 grams of thick yogurt)
-1/2 tsp vanilla essense
-140 grams maida
-100 grams caster sugar
-1/4 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp baking soda
-pinch of salt
-1/4 tsp cinnamon + pinch of nutmeg OR clove
-50 grams chocolate chips
-60 grams hazelnuts, roasted and chopped ( not too fine, allow for chunks)

Method: 
-whisk coffee+ milk + egg + vanilla extract
-in a large bowl, sift together he flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and spices 
-add in the chocolate chips and roasted hazelnuts
-to the dry mix, add in your coffee mix and mix together till a dough forms\
-create a log out of the dough and transfer the log to a parchment paper lined baking sheet
-bake in a preheated 200”C for about 30 minutes or until firm to the touch, note the log will spread during baking)
- Remove from oven and cool for about 5 minutes.
-Reduce the temp to 150” C. 
-cut the log into 12 -15 pieces depending on the size you prefer
-arrange on a baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes on each side
-cool and store in an airtight container. should last you 2-3 weeks

Matar Paneer Recipe
(Peas & Cottage Cheese Curry)
a quintessential indian comfort food i grew up eating! 
F:20 | C:17 | P:14 

Recipe: 
Masala Paste:
15 cashews
6 black peppercorns
3 cloves
2 green cardamom
4-6 sprigs of coriander leaves, i use the stems too for better flavour
2 medium tomatoes
1 onion
2 green chillies
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste

1 tbsp ghee
1 tsp jeera
1/4 tsp haldi
1 tsp red chilli powder
1/2 tsp garam masala
120 grams green peas ( i use frozen) 
1 cup water
200 - 250 grams paneer, cubed
pinch of salt
1 tsp kasturi methi, crushed
coriander leaves

Method: 
Start by blending together all the ingredients for the masala paste till smooth. 
In a pressure cooker, heat ghee (use oil to make this vegan), Add 1 tsp cumin and saute till it becomes aromatic.
Then add in your Masala Paste and cook for 10 – 15 minutes (the more you cook this paste, the flavours will develop more. Once the paste has thickened and become a deeper colour, add in ¼ tsp haldi + 1 tsp red chilli powder + ½ tsp garam masala powder and combine.
Follow that up by adding 120 grams of green peas (I use Safal frozen) + 1 cup water, use more if you like a thinner gravy and pressure cook the mix for 10 minutes / 3 whistles. Let the cooker release on its own and stir the gravy. Add in a pinch of Salt and 200 grams Paneer - I’ve used @idfreshfood ( use Tofu to make this Vegan) + 1 tsp crushed kasturi methi. Serve with a sprinkle of coriander leaves!

Triple Chocolate Muffins
Calories: 280 per muffin
makes 8
F: 15 | P: 5 | C: 35

Ingredients: 
Dry:
-125 grams maida
-20 grams cocoa powder
-1/2 tsp baking soda
-salt, pinch
-100 grams caster sugar

Wet:
-1 egg
-90 grams yogurt 
-60 grams oil
-60 grams milk
-1 tsp vanilla essense

Mix in:

The Holi Cookie 
a thandai flavoured cookie dough with “holi”special chocolate chips

this cookie came to me in a dream so i had to recreate it! didnt have the time to find some ingredients so made the most basic small batch cookies you will ever find on the internet! and they are eggles #indianholiday 

makes 5 cookies; 70 grams each

Ingredients: 
for the base:
- 50 grams butter, softened 
- 30 grams brown sugar
- 30 grams caster sugar
- 2 tbsp milk (mix in 1/2 - 1 tbsp thandai powder) 

Dry: 
- 120 grams AP flour, sifted is ALWAYS better
- pinch baking soda
- 1/2 tsp salt

Mix ins: 
180 grams white chocolate, melted and coloured then repiped to form chocolate chips 
you can use walnuts, hazelnuts, pistachios etc as per your preference :)

Method: 

- add all your dry ingredients together, seive them and set aside
- cream your butter slightly with a spatula and then add in your sugars and bring together
-follow that up with your thandai milk and mix to combine
- gently sift in your dry ingredients and form the cookie dough
-add in your coloured white chocolate chips and fold together. 
- scoop out one ice cream scoop size of dough
- refridgetate your dough balls for around 40 minutes till slightly firm. 
- preheat your oven at 170 degrees C
- bake in the oven for 10 - 14 minutes. keep checking your cookies after the 8 minute mask and when the sides seem to be firming up and the centre is still soft, take them out and add 2 - 3 chocolate chips on each cookie for that final presentation ummmphh! 
- THE HARDEST PART: leave them to cool for 15 minutes on the sheet and dig in ;)

Dal Fry Recipe
this recipe serves around 4-5 people so can easily be halved for your 2 person household! 

Ingredients + Method ( all together so you can cook 

Pressure Cook Dal first
-120 grams Masoor Dal, washed then soaked for 30 minutes followed by a 3-4 whistle pressure cook
-Pressure cook with 1/2 tsp haldi (turmeric powder) + 1 tsp ghee + pinch of hing
-use the finger meethod to determine the amount of water - the water level should be as much as the first cut on your finger when dipped in 
-pressure cook for 3 whistles and allow the cooker to release

For the Masala:
add 1 tbsp ghee/oil for a vegan option to your saucepan 
add to that 1 large onions, finely chopped along with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste eachand 3 green chillies ( 1 finely chopped + 2 sliced in half) along with 1 stick of curry leaves, plucked  till soft and the onion goes translucent 
follow that up with pinch of hing +1 tsp turmeric powder (haldi) + 1 tsp red chilli powder + 1 tsp coriander powder ( im obsessed with this ingredient and will never not use it) and cook for 5 minutes to allow the masala to bhuno ( basically cook slightly in your onion mix) if you feel your masala sticking to the pot at this point, put in either 2 ice cubes or some water ( eye ball it just enough to get it not stick) 
then add in 2 large tomatoes, finely chopped - this will complete “deglaze” the pan of the masalas and it will come together. at this point, ideally you dont need to add water but if you actually feel like it is sticking a few tbsp will work. allow it to cook for 10 minutes till the tomatoes are super soft and add in salt, to taste
add in your cooked dal along with 1/2 or 1 cup of water depending on how thick or thin you want your dal ( i go with 1/2 cup because thick dal FTW always) 
follow that up with 1.5 tsp garam masala and cook for 5-10 minutes. once done, add in 1 tbsp kasturi methi  and switch off the heat. 
juice of one lemon, just before you eat the dal 
bunch of coriander leaves, chopped

1 cup dahi + 2 tbsp besan (gram flour) + 1 cup water
1 tsp ghee
1/2 tsp jeera 
1 onion, finely chopped
1 tsp ginger paste + 1 tsp garlic paste
2 green chillies, finely chopped
a few curry leaves
1/2 tsp red chilli powder
1/2 tsp haldi
1/2 tsp coriander powder
1/2 cup water, to thin out your curd besan mix while cooking 
salt, to taste
handful of coriander leaves, to garnish

Method: 
boil, peel and chop your aloo’s you can even mash them too randomly
mix curd with besan and thin with water set aside
in a pan, add the ghee then the jeera and mix 
add in the onions, ginger garlic pastes chillies and mixxxx let the onions go nice and translucent 
add in the tomato followed by the masalas 
let this cook for 5-10 minutes till tomatoes are mushy 
add in the aloo and mix together with the masalas 
before you add in the dahi mix, either drop your flame to low or switch it off like i did then add in the dahi besan mix and stir together, restart the flame and the mix will deepen colour to a deep yellow, add in 1/2 cup water to thin out and then salt to taste 
should take 10-20 minutes you want the raw besan flavour to be gone
serve with chopped coriander | serve with rice or roti and enjoy :)

Brioche Hot Dog Buns
i wanted a hot dog and couldnt find buns so my best friend told me to make these from scratch hence began this 2 hour journey

Ingredients: 
350 grams maida
1 tbsp sugar
1 tsp active dry yeast
1 tsp salt
2 eggs
110 ml milk
55 grams butter, soft, at room tempreture

Method: 
combine flour, sugar, salt and yeast in a bowl, add in your eggs and room temp milk (it shouldnt be too hot or cold or your yeast goes bye bye)
kneed for 5 minutes then add in the butter and knead for another 5 mins
leave it to proof for 40-60 minutes till it doubles in size
take it out and divide into 6 equal portions
i rolled them the best i could, ideally roll to a cylinder and then roll them onto themselves
leave to proof for 30 mins on a tray, then add some egg wash sesame seeds and bake at 180 degrees for 20 minutes or till done 
these keep well in the fridge for 2-3 days and can be warmed in a microwave to get them soft again

Chocolate Soufflé Recipe 
Indulge in the ultimate chocolate experience with our heavenly Chocolate Soufflé. It’s pure decadence in every bite!

Macros:
C: 31 | F: 22 | P: 8
Calories: 354 per portion 
Makes 3

Ingredients: 
-57 ml milk
-30 grams sugar, divided equally ( half for custard mix + half to whip egg whites)
-pinch of salt
-1 tbsp maida
-15 grams butter, cubed, if using salted butter, omit salt from the recipe
-80 grams chocolate, 70% and up works best
-2 eggs, seperated
-1/2 tsp vanilla essense
-pinch of cream of tartare, skip if you do not have
-butter + caster sugar for buttering and dusting the ramekin

Method:
-using a pastry brush, brush the ramekins with butter and add the sugar moving it around till the bottom and sides are evenly coated
-add flour + sugar + salt to a saucepan, add in milk and stir together till combined, then add in the butter and stir on a low flame till everything is disolved and slightly thickened. 
-add in your chopped chocolate and stir till melted and combined, allow to cool slightly before adding in your egg yolks. once combined, leave to cool
-in another bowl, add your egg whites + cream of tartare. whip your egg whites while gradually adding in the 15 grams of sugar till you achieve stiff peaks
-fold the egg whites into the chocolate custard in 2 parts folding the mixture gently so you dont reflate it too much
-add your mix to the ramekins and bake in a preheated oven (190°C) for 10-12 minutes or until your souffle has risen well and is not jiggly
-remove from the oven and serve immediately

Nutella French Toast
a quick cheats breakfast that comes together in 10 minutes
F:9 | C:41 | P:10
Ingredients:
8 slices of bread, i use wholewheat bread, use a thick bread if possible ( brioche is the best) 
2 eggs
1 cup milk, whole or skimmed 
1 tbsp sugar
pinch of salt
1/2 tsp cinnamon powder
4 tbsp nutella
a little butter to fry the french toast

Method: 
Mix all your ingredients in a bowl except the bread and nutella
spread 1 tbsp of nutella to a slice of bread and top with another slice
dip in the egg mix on both sides (20 seconds each till it absorbs well but still keeps its shape)
place your frying pan on medium heat and melt a little butter
add in your french toast and cook on both sides till golden brown
remove and serve it fresh :) 

add ons: whipped cream, maple syrup,

heathy pro tip: sub 1 tbsp of sugar for monk fruit / add 1 tbsp protein powder to the mix/ sub nutella for pieces of 70% and above dark chocolate (they melt well too)

Palak Khichdi
meal prep friendly

another simple dal khichdi recipe but today im using another ingredient lying in my fridge - spinach! 
this is my go to meal when i dont want to spend more than 10 minutes in the kitchen actively cooking in my kitchen! 

Nutrition: 
C: 71 | F: 5 | P: 18
Calories: 394 per portion 
Makes 2 portions (can be extended to serve 3 medium sized portions with a hearty subzi)

Ingredients: 
80 grams basmati rice + 100 grams dal (toor or masoor), rinsed till water runs clear and soaked for 30 minutes 
1 tsp jeera seeds
pinch of hing
1 onion, finely chopped
1 tsp ginger garlic paste + add in more finely minced garlic for extra flavour
2 tomato, finely chopped
2 green chillies, finely chopped
250 grams spinach, blanced and pureed with 1/4 cup water
1/2 tsp haldi
1 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
1 tsp garam masala
1 tsp coriander powder
salt, to taste
around 400 ml water, should completely submerge 

-Chopped coriander, for garnish

Method: 
add your ghee to the pressure cooker followed by the cumin seeds and stir together
add in the onion, ggp paste, chilli and cook till onions are translucent
add in all the masalas and stir for a few minutes, it gets dry and can burn so add in a few tbsp of water
add in the tomatoes and cook for a few minutes, add in your spinach puree at this point
then add in your dal + rice and stir for 2-3 minutes,
pour in the water and pressure cook on low for 3 whistles 
allow the pressure cooker to release then open mix together, add the salt and stir in your fresh coriander at the end 
enjoy :)

Ingredients
140 grams dark chocolate, chopped
80 grams butter, cubed
2 eggs
160 grams caster sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract
60 grams maida
10 grams cocoa powder
100 grams dark chocolate

Method: 
melt the butter and chocolate in a bowl in the microwave in 30 second intervals, stiring each time
in another bowl, add the eggs and caster sugar together and whip till its light and fluffy (video shows the consistency)
add the melted butter-chocolate mix to the above mix and fold together gently, you dont want to release all the air you whipped into the egg sugar mix
sift in the maida and cocoa powder and fold together 
add in the chopped chocolate  and combine
add to your lined baking dish and top with sea salt 
bake at 180 degrees C for 20-35 minutes
timing will never be the same depending on your oven and it will vary start checking around the 20-25 minute mark and when you insert a knife in, it should come out with moist crumbs. 
if it comes out clean, its overbaked, if it comes out as wet batter, its not ready yet

Dish needed: 7 inch baking dish

Matar Paneer Recipe
(Peas & Cottage Cheese Curry)
a quintessential indian comfort food i grew up eating! 

Nutrition: 
C: 17 | F: 20 | P: 15
Calories: 295 for this recipe
Serves 4

Ingredients
Masala Paste:
15 cashews
6 black peppercorns
3 cloves
2 green cardamom
4-6 sprigs of coriander leaves, i use the stems too for better flavour
2 medium tomatoes
1 onion
2 green chillies
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste

1 tbsp ghee
1 tsp jeera
1/4 tsp haldi
1 tsp red chilli powder
1/2 tsp garam masala
120 grams green peas ( i use frozen) 
1 cup water
200 - 250 grams paneer, cubed
pinch of salt
1 tsp kasturi methi, crushed
coriander leaves

Method: 
Start by blending together all the ingredients for the masala paste till smooth. 
In a pressure cooker, heat ghee (use oil to make this vegan), Add 1 tsp cumin and saute till it becomes aromatic.
Then add in your Masala Paste and cook for 10 – 15 minutes (the more you cook this paste, the flavours will develop more. Once the paste has thickened and become a deeper colour, add in tsp haldi + red chilli powder + garam masala powder and combine.
Follow that up by adding in the green peas (I use Safal frozen) + water, use more if you like a thinner gravy and pressure cook the mix for 10 minutes / 3 whistles. Let the cooker release on its own and stir the gravy. 
Add in a pinch of Salt and cubed paneer  ( use Tofu to make this Vegan) + crushed kasturi methi. Serve with a sprinkle of coriander leaves!

Nutrition:

50 grams caster sugar

160 grams maida

1/2 tsp baking soda
1/2 tsp coffee powder
pinch of salt

150 grams dark chocolate chunks 

Method
cream the butter with both the sugar till fluffy 
add in the egg or yogurt and vanilla and mix together

the cookies should not be fully set they should be slightly set but will still be soft to touch in the oven and once they come out they have more structure as they cool 
the longer you bake the crunchier they will be 
once cooled, store in an airtight container for 2-4 days

Spices and ingredients also vary significantly between North and South Indian cuisines. While we use a lot of garam masalas in the North, South Indian cooking relies heavily on ingredients like curry leaves, mustard seeds and coconut, along with its own myriad of spice mixes. Another aspect of South Indian cooking that fascinated me was the variety of chutneys, curries and podis that accompany and flavour meals. Each region in South India has its own unique versions and mastering them has become a point of pride for me.

Over time, I’ve come to appreciate the intricacies of South Indian cuisine and have gained the confidence to prepare dishes like sambar, rasam, and lesser known and commercialised items. These tombs are a testament to the Qutub Shahi dynasty’s architectural and cultural legacy in the region. The complex houses the tombs of several rulers of the dynasty, including that of Sultan Quli Qutub Shah, the founder of Hyderabad. incredible right? 
As you explore the tombs, you’ll be struck by the stunning Indo-Islamic architecture, featuring intricate stone carvings, graceful arches, and ornate domes. The tombs are a remarkable blend of Persian, Hindu, and Pathan architectural influences, making them unique in their design.
The peaceful ambiance of the gardens surrounding the tombs provides a serene backdrop for your visit. It’s a place where you can take a leisurely stroll and appreciate the historical significance and architectural beauty of the site. The tombs are often bathed in soft, golden light during the evening, creating a magical atmosphere.

Overall, a visit to the Shahi Qutub Tombs in Hyderabad offers a glimpse into the rich history and culture of the region, making it a must-see attraction for history enthusiasts and anyone interested in the architectural marvels of India.

1 tbsp rice flour mixed with 1/4 cup water

Method 
prep work: add the tamarind to a bowl and top with 3 cups hot water and set aside for 30 minutes
squeeze the tamarind with the water once its warm to touch and then drain the water squeezing out the tamarind goodness and set aside 
in a pan add oil to the pan then the mustard seeds, chana dal and urad dal and let it cook - the seeds will splutter and the dals will be mildly brown - dont let it burn 
add in the garllic cloves and the shallots ( if you feel the shallots are big, then you can cut them in half too , they simmer in the gravy so well ) 
once a few minutes of saute is done, add in the kozhambu podi and tamarind water and combine 
this will now simmer for 20-30 minutes
once thats done add in the sugar / jaggery + rice flour mix and let it thicken 
this will take 2-4 minutes, then add salt to taste and its ready 
Serving: 
this is a very tangy gravy so its eaten with rice but don’t serve it to yourself like you would a dal as it can be overpowering
tastes great with a large serving of rice and a ladel or two of this kozhambu 
Note: 
this is not the most traditional style vatha kozhamabu that usually uses Sundakkai in the recipe but i didnt have it and ive seen more detailed recipes with alot more steps but this is the recipe my mother in law showed me and i follow it!

once it begins to simmer, turn off the heat

in a small pan, make the tadka with the ingredients mentioned in the caption 
add to the curry and and cover for 5 minutes

paste

marinate the chicken for a minimum of 30 minutes

Dal Makhani

Nutrition: ( as calculated on myfitnesspal ) 
C: 30 | F: 7 | P: 11
Calories: 240 per serve
Serves 5 - 6

Ingredients
1 cup urad dal ( black lentils ) ( 200 grams ) 
1/4 cup rajma ( 50 grams ) 
1/2 tsp salt

1 tbsp butter
1/2 tbsp oil 
2 tbsp ginger garlic paste
1 tbsp red chilli paste ( use between 1 - 2 tbsp depending on how spicy you want it ) 
1/2 tsp garam masala
6 tomatoes, blended well
salt, to taste 
2 tbsp fresh cream ( 40 grams ) 
1 tbsp kasturi methi
pinch of garam masala 

to garnish 
5 grams butter
1 - 2 tbsp cream 

Method 
rinse the urad dal and rajma well till the water runs clear and soak overnight 
the next day, in a pressure cooker, add the mix to a pressure cooker, add 2 cups water and let it boil for 10 minutes, you will see scum on the top that you can remove with a ladel 
then pressure cook for 6 whistles 
let the pressure release and open the cooker, mash the mix with a potato masher for a minute, set aside

in a kadhai, add in butter + oil followed by the ginger garlic paste and stir 
add in the red chilli powder and garam masala and combine 
blend the tomatoes in a blender and add to the kadhai and combine with the paste and cook for a few minutes 
add in the mashed dal along with salt and cook adding in a cup of water 
i usually cook this for 20-30 minutes for the best melt in your mouth experience then add in the cream followed by kasturi methi and garam masala 
cook it for a few more minutes and serve with a drizzle of cream and a little butter for the melty look

Serves 3

Ingredients

temper 
1/2 tbsp ghee/ oil

2 cloves
8-10 curry leaves

Method 
combine besan & yogurt in a bowl. gradually add water and whisk until achieving a lump-free, smooth mixture.

once ready, garnish with chopped coriander. 

serve Gujarati kadhi hot or warm alongside steamed rice  ideally accompanied by a vegetable side dish, pickle, and salad.

Ancient City, Bangkok

Share this with someeone going to Bangkok soon :) 

Situated beyond the bustling streets of Bangkok, along the old route leading to the Pattaya beach resort, lies a somewhat lesser-known treasure – the “Ancient City” (Muang Boran in Thai), a park dedicated to the preservation of Thailand’s cultural heritage.
Established by a now-deceased affluent Thai billionaire, this expansive 320-acre park, mimicking the shape of Thailand itself, serves as a homage to the nation’s rich history. The Ancient City meticulously replicates, often on a smaller scale, significant edifices and historical sites from various corners of Thailand. 
With over 100 monuments, including both reconstructed structures and examples of traditional vernacular architecture saved from demolition, the park stands as a remarkable testament to the diverse and culturally significant landmarks throughout the country. A visit to this unique destination promises an immersive journey through Thailand’s past, offering a glimpse into the architectural marvels that define its rich cultural tapestry.

French Onion Chicken 
easy recipe | high protein | dinner for two | easy dinner | date night | meal prep friendly | valentines meal 

Nutrition: 
Macros: C: 18 | F: 13 | P: 51
Calories:  400 per serve 
Makes 3 

Ingredients
3 chicken breasts, pounded with a mallet to thin it and even it out ( around 450-500 grams ) 
seasoning: 
salt + black pepper + cajun seasoning 
1 tsp oil 
1 tbsp minced garlic
2 large onions, finely sliced or 4 medium onions 
1 1/2 cup chicken stock or vegetable stock is good too 
1 /2 tbsp cornflour / arrow root powder 
35 grams gruyère

Method 
start by prepping the chicken - mallet the breasts till they even out 
season with salt + pepper + seasoning of choice ( i use cajun seasoning )
set aside till ready to cook 

in a pan, add in oil, garlic and sliced onions, cook on high for a few minutes till you see some colour on them
add in 1/4 cup stock at this point and allow the onions to cook in it for a few minutes till the liquid is gone 
then let it cook till you have the desired colour you want, take it out into a bowl
in the same pan, add in your chicken and cook well on both sides - take it out 
you will see charred bits on the pan that is amazing for the sauce and will pack so much flavour - 
add the cooked onions back in the pan along with remaining stock + cornflour mix and stir stir stir - the charred bits will come off the pan and mix into the sauce giving it a deeper colour 
add the chicken back in and add some onions to the top then add on grated cheese and cover for a minute while the cheese melts

its ready to serve, i love it with mashed potatoes and a side salad or even rice or some crusty bread would be great :)

Air Fryer Chicken Parmesan

* 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
* 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
* 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
* 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
* 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
* 1/2 teaspoon dried basil
* 1/4 teaspoon salt
* 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
* 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
* 2 egg, beaten
* 1/2 cup marinara sauce
* 1/2 cup shredded Parmesan cheese
* Cooking spray
Instructions:
* Preheat your air fryer to 375°F (190°C).
* In a shallow dish, mix together breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, oregano, basil, salt, and black pepper.
* Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with the breadcrumb mixture.
* Coat each chicken breast in flour, shaking off any excess.
* Dip the chicken into the beaten egg, allowing any excess to drip off.
* Press the chicken into the breadcrumb mixture, coating it evenly on all sides.
* Spray the air fryer basket with cooking spray to prevent sticking.
* Place the breaded chicken breasts in the air fryer basket in a single layer, making sure they’re not touching each other.
* Cook in the air fryer for 10-12 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature reaches 165°F or 74°C).
* Remove the chicken from the air fryer and top each breast with marinara sauce and shredded mozzarella cheese.
* Return the chicken to the air fryer and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
* Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil or parsley or coriander if desired. Enjoy your air fryer chicken Parmesan with some pasta!

SWEET & SOUR PANEER 🍍
A sticky, glossy, sweet & sour paneer that takes barely any effort and tastes like takeout at home 🤌🏼

375 calories | 29g protein per serving

Macros are for the paneer + vegetables + sauce only and do not include udon, noodles or rice.
Serves 2

INGREDIENTS
Paneer & vegetables
* 200g paneer, cut into cubes
* 1 medium onion, cut into chunky pieces
* 1 capsicum, cut into chunky pieces
* 100g mushrooms, sliced
* 4–5 cloves garlic, finely chopped
* 1 tsp oil
* Sesame seeds, to garnish

Sweet & sour sauce ( feel free to adjust as per your taste - more/less spicy/salty)
* 200g pineapple juice
* 2 tbsp soy sauce
* 2 tbsp oyster sauce
* 1 tbsp chilli sauce
* 2 tsp vinegar
* 1 tbsp cornflour
* 1/2 cup water
METHOD
1. Add the pineapple juice, soy sauce, oyster sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar and cornflour to a bowl. Add water and whisk until completely smooth.
2. Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 20–30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Add the onion, capsicum and mushrooms and stir-fry on high heat for 3–4 minutes. Keep the vegetables slightly crisp.
4. Give the sauce another good whisk , the cornflour settles at the bottom  and pour it into the pan.
5. Add the cubed paneer directly to the pan and gently toss with the vegetables and sauce.
6. Toss everything together over medium-high heat until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy and sticky.
7. Serve over udon noodles like I did here, or with steamed rice, and finish with sesame seeds.

PRO TIP: Always whisk your sauce again right before adding it to the pan so the cornflour is evenly distributed and you get that gorgeous glossy coating.

Chicken
* 450g @licious_foods chicken mince

METHOD
